attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post.

semantics.note: Firm 'will' about the labs' capital needs. Keeps the 'as commitments begin' timing. Leaving out the Broadcom aside is acceptable; it is additive context, not the core forecast.

contract.note: Plain reading fits his words: as capacity comes online, cash needs jump sharply and in lumpy amounts. Reading 'as commitments begin' as timing is ordinary. He named no deadline, so the horizon is open.

evidence.note: OpenAI raising up to $30B after the post fits large capital needs. But it is framed as opportunistic and not tied to compute payments coming due.
About $600B of compute spend runs through 2030, so most of the ramp is still ahead and the test period has barely begun.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with no deadline. The only raise in the packet is described as opportunistic and is not linked to compute obligations. Most commitments fall later, through 2030. No filing shows payments stepping up alongside a forced financing, or the ramp being funded from operating cash. The early-resolution rule is not met, so this cannot be scored yet.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his own post.

semantics.note: The 'because' clause comes from his very next sentence, so the proposition stays within what he said. 'Artificial' is a characterization, and the claim is about AI startups as a group.

contract.note: Reducing 'artificial' to its checkable core (token spend funded by VC rather than operating cash flow, for the group as a whole) is an ordinary plain reading and fair to him.

evidence.note: Covers 2025, outside the target period. It shows top buyers include a VC-backed startup and a Microsoft product, but says nothing about how startups' token spend is funded.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no aggregate or representative data on whether AI startups pay the labs from venture funding or from operating cash flow in 2026. The single item covers a different period and does not address funding sources. The evidence neither supports nor contradicts the claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words. He draws on Ramp data but states the conclusion himself.

semantics.note: Keeps the 'likely hundreds' and 'indeterminately-large chunk' hedges. The firm parts are the 80% concentration and enterprise being the vast majority of total revenue.

contract.note: Scoring only the firm parts and leaving the hedged parts unscored is fair. Reading the 80% as the labs' real enterprise revenue matches what he said. Testing 'vast majority' at each lab is reasonable, since he wrote 'their'.

evidence.note: Ramp: the top 1% of customers account for 80% of enterprise revenue at both labs. It is an estimate drawn from Ramp's own sample.
Sacra estimates API at about 80% of Anthropic's total revenue, which supports 'vast majority' for Anthropic only.
OpenAI's enterprise revenue only just passed consumer by Aug 2026, about half of total and not a vast majority. Anonymously sourced.
OpenAI discloses no customer-level revenue concentration, so the Ramp figure cannot be checked against company data.

reviews.rationale: The 80% concentration is supported for both labs by Ramp's estimate. 'Vast majority of total revenue' holds for Anthropic (about 80% API) but not for OpenAI, where enterprise only just passed half in Aug 2026. That meets the contract's 'roughly half' contradiction test. Combined across both labs, the share is also not a vast majority.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sidenote in his own post.

semantics.note: Framed as his own estimate, with the stated hedge that the figure could be smaller. Both the estimate framing and the hedge are preserved.

contract.note: The measure is undefined, no period is given beyond 'annual', and he explicitly left the downside open. Declining to grade is fair to his words.

reviews.rationale: This is a hedged personal estimate ('could be smaller') of an undefined metric, 'AI compute demand', with no defined period. There is no fair threshold to test, and the packet contains no evidence items. Not scored.
